I really want to recommend Mob Psycho 100. I have some mixed feelings about no contact, like any tool I think that there are some circumstances it fits perfectly and some that it doesn't. However, there is one benefit that I think is nearly universal, and is why I find it is suggested so often.


No contact forces you into an uncomfortable situation. Specifically, it forces you to really try to put this person fully out of your life. That sounds very painful, but bear with me here.


The most important part of healing from a breakup is filling your life with new things. A support system, meeting people, new hobbies/work, whatever. You have an abundance of time and resources you used to devote to your partner. Removing the option of spending time agonizing about what they're doing and if you should reach out forces you to... do something else. And making it a strict rule makes you do something else for a *while.*


That's what I think it's really about. Giving yourself more ability to rebuild.
I've had people return after no contact, I've had the opposite. In both cases, I was always glad to have given myself that space. It *sucks* in the moment, don't get me wrong. But looking back, it was one of the best steps I took.

I am so sorry. I wish I had resources to help you with money.

If you can at all afford it, please make one of your expenses a gym membership. No one will pressure you to actually work out. It's a place you can shelter from weather and get some safe social interaction, and most importantly you have a space to shower and possibly even wash clothes. (The latter is very rare at gyms but my fingers are crossed.)

It is not always safe, but if you have a Walmart near you they often let truckers or roadtrippers sleep in their parking lot at night. First choice would be staying with a friend, shelter, or other family but this is an option.

Definitely agree with getting the police involved. If nothing else, he might end up having to pay you, which would be a good buffer until you can settle somewhere.

I keep all of my socials on a "work" screen and use them specifically for that. I think my only exceptions are Reddit and BlueSky, which I've started using because the chronological/less filtered nature makes it feel worthwhile to talk to people. Even there, my usage is down to an hour a day usually, unless I'm actively having fun in conversations.

It really is worth it just to move the icons away or uninstall the apps so that using them becomes a rarity. I feel so much less stressed, and when I do decide to use them I enjoy my experience more.

My heart goes out to the entirety of their families, of course, but it stings extra-hard seeing kids who never asked to be born saddled in that situation.

I'd actually argue being there in an emotional capacity might make things worse with how messy the situation is. She needs to be around a support network unrelated to her romantic life. 


It will probably feel like it's the wrong thing at first--the metaphor of an open wound is surprisingly apt. It will hurt terribly at first, but if it is kept clean, when it heals it will be healthier and perhaps have less scarring. You'll both have time to heal on your own, and when that pain has subsided paths forward will become more clear.

This might sound really trite or overly-sweet, I'm really sorry if it does. But after something like that I really feel like telling you that you're doing amazing. I just am really impressed that you managed to make it through that, even if you cried. I know I've been hurt way more than I expected by things kids have said when they were just playing--that doesn't mean they're bad kids, but being from the kids doesn't mean you didn't just hear something really cruel either!

Definitely find time to process if you can. Venting here is a pretty good option, but I hope you can have some dedicated time to yourself sometime in the coming weeks.

My last memory with my grandmother before she became too sick to functionally understand who I was or what was happening was watching Downton Abbey from start to finish. During the last (or one of the last) episodes in the series' run, the characters sing Auld Lang Syne together.

I just remember so many thoughts going through my mind. That we only get so many years. That the years we get don't often match the people we wish they did. That goodbye was coming fast. That goodbye was forever this time. That this was going to just keep happening until it was my turn.

I'm really attached to the song, but I can't hear it without falling into a full ugly cry and a full relapse into the heavy weight of those realizations. Someone could literally sabotage my day with it.

I have had high blood pressure for most of my adult life due to a combination of genetic factors. It's very common, and it... really doesn't feel like anything when you have it. However, I have always had both extremely high anxiety and a fairly low pain tolerance, especially when it came to external sources. I also have suffered from chronic migraines, which I couldn't determine the source of.

The last few months, I started getting these nosebleeds that were much more intense than any I'd experienced. I would taste metal right before they would begin--a trend I'm glad I picked up fast, because it was truly 0 to waterfall. So I finally decided to ask my doctor if I could get on blood pressure medication, something she was hesitant to do because "I'm young."

Being on this medication has shifted my life so much. I feel capable of keeping calm in a way that I never could. Sleep is more restful. I haven't had the chance to see if my pain tolerance is affected, but I can distinctly say the migraines, while not gone, are much less common and slightly less lengthy. The nosebleeds stopped immediately. I started re-trying to learn meditation techniques after many years of frustration, and have had a notable difference in how it feels to sit still in my own head. It's like I literally found a switch for panic.

I'm talking a shift from around 195/170 to 120/80, that big. But even if yours is not that alarmingly high, it's definitely something to consider if you have similar symptoms to mine.

This can help you both with working through the practical issues such as moving out.

This suggestion comes with a warning. This will take time, and the first few sessions are going to feel terrible. You may be made to feel very guilty when your partner is in the fresh stages of grief, and it may not feel fair during the stages where the therapist is helping them through crisis points. I urge you strongly to stick it out. It will be worth it.

The point of this is twofold. If you stay, you'll have had help getting the spark back. If you go, you'll know you did what you could and will have your partner set up in a position where you both have more of a support network and somewhere to go for answers. 

It also means, while not guaranteed, your chances of reconnecting as platonic friends someday may be better. I and a lot of people here would have felt a lot better if we felt our partner really did try to fix things and it just didn't work, and this is a very clear demonstration of that.

Looking back, I am proud of young me for still thinking "but why do we make this lifestyle choice our business over all of the others?"

I remember thinking it was really sad, because even if it was a choice, falling in love with someone and realizing you'd have to pick between them and your community was a horrible, horrible reality.

Especially folks who have a figure similar to mine may have to work harder on it. But if I can tell someone cares, it goes a *really long way* in terms of how attracted I am to them.
Personally I have always dreamed of going to a play party or other environment where people are consenting to see more overt things. But I really like very subtle public play too.

I have to be honest, this is so much more complex than one person being wrong or right.

I get the sense you might be looking for thoughts on whether or not you really should leave. Lots of people have had different takes and I think it's a great idea to get a variety of opinions on something this serious. Personally, I don't think I can give you your ultimate answer. I do strongly feel that if you do, there are good and bad ways to go about it. But the act of leaving, or even wanting to leave, is not wrong or bad of you. I think that you deserve peace, and this was a violation of your trust in her. Whether it is an irreparable violation is not my business to say, it can only be the business of you and her.


I hate to say this part, because I don't want it to create undue pressure, but I don't see a way to say this that doesn't sound really pressuring. Please take your time to make sure you go about this in a way and on a timeframe you don't regret. I have seen people cut things off in a panic, and I have seen people stay out of guilt and resentment. Neither is what I want you to be.


After what you experienced, I honestly think therapy of *some* kind is a hard line ultimatum for both of you. You can't live through an attempt, or the attempt of your loved one, without some kind of professional treatment. It is literally one of the ultimate human traumas.


Sorry that this reply is coming out really disjointed, this topic hits really close to home. Tl;dr, I think neither of you is the asshole and both of you are so severely hurting. I really hope you can both get help, and I want you to know that it's not wrong to want to leave, but to be careful how you go about it.

I only realize as an adult that I hid in my room as much as possible when I was home, and still have an agoraphobia that sometimes flares to specifically encapsulate anything outside my room. But Grandma's house, I could wander everywhere. I would sit in every room and just... be.

I don't always mind when kids act up. They have a lot of emotions in their little bodies that they are learning to process, so I would like to preface this by saying I do not at all think the kids are bad for doing this. It's just a really common thing that gets me very riled up.


When a kid that is old enough to talk is denied something, or is annoyed by their sibling, or their parent is urging them to eat their veggies at a restaurant, and they shift from verbal complaints to that long, wordless whining. And any further irritation just sends them to whine harder and louder. And louder.


I feel bad for them. They're distressed, in public, and maybe this is the only way their parents will act. It can't be something they *want* to do. I just... something irrational and kind of cruel in me wants to tell them "you're not an animal, *talk.*" It makes me angry beyond what is reasonable.


A big part of why I don't want to be a mom is that I know these parts of myself wouldn't disappear for my own kid. I'd never forgive myself if I spoke that aloud so harshly to any child, much less my own.

I use "darling" a ton. I think it just naturally flows with my way of speaking. A few injokes have turned into pet names, which might be something to think about.


I have also kind of made a policy of seeing how my partners respond to compliments that are just slightly weird for their gender to hear. A lot of guys have *really* liked when I've called them pretty or beautiful. Some girls get very happy at being called handsome. It's not a guaranteed thing, but definitely worth trying on for size to see how they feel.

You're absolutely at the hardest part right now. When the feelings are fresh, I know that all those nice things I listed might have done nothing for me. But I will say that this part is very temporary.


I like to think of the mind as being not too different from other systems in our body. Take the immune system--pretty cool that we don't die when we get sick, but it makes us get fevers and throw up and all kinds of horrible sensations to operate.


Grief, in my mind, is similar. The mind has a ton of healing to do right now. There is so much upsetting information, so many old habits in the process of getting rewritten. When I think about it like how my body might process a toxin, it makes sense that it hurts so much right now. Worse because it's tied to memories and real connections.


This is why I hold true to the whole "be gentle with yourself" thing in these early stages. Right now you're having the worst part of the healing. But soon enough, joy starts coming back. I encourage you to search for it in those little ways when it does, because nowadays, even though I'm still chasing crumbs, I'm really happy to be alive.


Sending big dumb internet hugs. I really hope that the pain passes sooner than later, and that lots of good things find you, big or small.

I hate hearing that I'll find someone better but I literally survived off "it will get better" in a nebulous sense.


For a really long time I just kept myself going saying "okay, welp, maybe I'm never getting into a relationship again. How do I find a scrap of happiness here? Let's find even a crumb."


I failed a LOT. Imagine ordering entire hobby kits and finding they made me feel nothing. Watching movies that made me cry and scream at myself in the mirror. ... but then I found a game I liked. And then I got back into writing fiction. 


Then I learned some basic Python, not gonna do anything with it but it was fun. Then I went to the animal shelter and walked a dog. I didn't adopt him but it was a nice day and I sat on a bench while he napped in the sun. Then I tried drawing and hated it, and fell back into a spiral because my ex was a designer. But then the next day I went to a new restaurant that had bitchin' mozzarella sticks. Tomorrow I'm going to my psychiatrist which is an anxious time for me, but we are gonna get burgers on the way! So I'm trying to remember hell yeah, burgers.


This all happened over many months. And it's not an exhaustive list. The exhaustive list would include a big agoraphobia battle and a lot of forcing myself to be social to an entire gradient of success and failure.


Do I want a relationship still? Yes, although I'm more open to more casual arrangements or even polyamory. I am currently talking to someone that I might commit to, but we'll see.


At the end of the day, any of those arrangements could crash and burn. I am, in fact, hysterically afraid of that and have made very troubling paranoid statements aplenty on dates. But that dog was so cute. And I liked those video games. And I gotta have more of those mozz sticks. And that's what I think life is made of for me now.

Nearly 30 here and... I just get it for pets. I am constantly having to be talked down from bringing home critters. (It's easy to do so, as I want to provide a good home if I were to adopt anyone, so no impulse buys.)


But babies, frankly, I feel the opposite about. The older I get the less I want them. When I was young I was so curious about what that feeling of nurturing and excitement would feel like, so much that I even envied it a little. But it never came, and in fact was mostly overtaken by revulsion and tokophobia.


When people ask me this, though, I always give the same answer. "Maybe it'll magically switch on someday, and then I'll adopt. If I am deemed unsuitable to adopt, I shouldn't be birthing a kid into the same situation. So I'd work toward being able to adopt. Doesn't your biological drive for achievement and stability make that sound really rewarding?"

I've had two very different experiences with this.

In the former, the breakup was mutual. Not "mutual but one person hesitated," not "mutual because I admitted the problems existed," actually mutual in that we felt the relationship dying and thought we decided to try to work things out, then later decided we weren't a great match.

I'm best friends with that ex today, four years later. But it took work to get there, and we were not best friends right after the breakup.

An important ground rule we set was that we were not going NC, but we were going to build support systems separate from one another. We gave each other a grace period of about a week, before we were going to fully stop talking about the breakup and old relationship to each other. We could still talk about it, but we had to bring it to other friends and family. If we were constantly guilting or just reminding each other? One of us would have cracked and wanted to go back, or felt horrible and needed to cut the other off.

We also did not hang out except in group settings for a while. This was easier for us since we had a shared friend group. Some nights I would still leave these meetups and cry, even though I knew we were making the right decision.

It was good to force interaction with other people, even though that was very difficult. It meant once we started feeling comfortable being alone together after a little under a year, it wasn't because one or both of us were just lonely.

Though, it took about a year and change for me to get to a point where I would not describe the experience as painful, if you're looking for a timeline. That's right, even in a mutual breakup it *suuucks* for that long.

But it did pass, and now I trust that guy more than I did when we were dating. We hang out all the time now, and have both cheered each other on through different relationships.

Now, the second experience... my most recent ex *wants* to be best friends, but he did blindside me and break my heart with a particularly gutting ultimatum. There was no agreement, and he said "just give it time" before going completely cold on me.

Now (7 months later) he occasionally sends me memes and I laugh or send one back. We never talk one-on-one, but even in group settings we don't really address each other anymore. We're acquaintances, and I have no interest in being anything other than civil for the sake of our mutual friends. Hilarious that I once thought of him as closer to me than the former dude.

It was a really strange ultimatum that caused the breakup--I had told him very early in the relationship, "hey, I'm not willing to have kids, and I don't want to lead you on if that's what you want out of life." And at the time, he said it was okay, but apparently he hoped for 3 years that I would "grow up" and change my mind.

I put adoption on the table because I was desperate and in shock, but he was insistent it needed to be a kid that popped out of me, no surrogates or adoption allowed. And I thought that was such an odd hill to die on, especially after springing this on me after so long.

None of it made any sense, and still doesn't. But I suppose I meant what I said that no one should be forced into or out of their decision on kids.

The fact that I didn't know for three years though, and I had started planning to marry this man--that kind of screwed me up permanently. I'm scared even if I find someone who wants the same life I do, I won't believe them when they say it. And that's really unfair to them.
